title: Dynamical many-body control of high harmonic generation in a Mott insulator
authors: Mingyao Guo, Ryo Noguchi, Mohammad Muntasir Hassan, Steven J. Gomez Alvarado, Reina M. Gomez, Yao-Jui Chan, Yu-Chieh Wen, Stephen D. Wilson, Yao Wang, David Hsieh
abstract: High harmonic generation (HHG) has emerged as a powerful probe of ultrafast electron dynamics in solids. However, in strongly correlated materials, where electronic excitations arise from many-body interactions rather than single-particle band dispersion, the field remains in its infancy. Here, we report HHG up to the 23$^{rd}$ order in the prototypical Mott insulator La$_2$CuO$_4$. We observe a robust 4 eV cutoff that is independent of driving field strength, revealing an intrinsic energy scale defined by the Hubbard bands. Using time-resolved high harmonic spectroscopy, we disentangle the distinct contributions of carrier creation, intraband acceleration, and interband recombination to the nonequilibrium radiation spectrum. We demonstrate that photo-doping triggers a fundamental reorganization of the many-body manifolds above a critical excitation density, a process that renormalizes the band curvature and suppresses nonlinear intraband currents, thereby directly imprinting the signature of many-body band reconstruction onto the harmonic emission. These results establish HHG as a sensitive probe of subtle correlation-driven electronic reconstructions and highlight that many-body interactions enable extreme nonlinear optical responses that are highly tunable in nonequilibrium states.
summary: This paper uses High Harmonic Generation (HHG) spectroscopy on a Mott insulator to study ultrafast electron dynamics. By analyzing the harmonic spectrum, the authors show that photo-doping causes a fundamental reorganization of the electronic structure, which manifests as a distinct change in the nonlinear optical response. This establishes HHG as a highly sensitive probe for correlation-driven electronic reconstructions in strongly correlated materials.
main_problem: The study investigates how High Harmonic Generation (HHG) can serve as a sensitive probe to characterize ultrafast electron dynamics and the fundamental electronic reconstructions occurring in strongly correlated Mott insulators.
main_result: The research demonstrates that photo-doping triggers a fundamental reorganization of the many-body electronic manifolds, evidenced by the suppression of interband recombination channels and the renormalization of band curvature, which is directly imprinted onto the HHG spectrum.
method: The authors combine time-resolved HHG spectroscopy on cuprate Mott insulators with detailed numerical simulations using the Hubbard model to disentangle intraband and interband contributions to the nonlinear optical response.
model_or_system: The system is a Mott insulator, exemplified by La2CuO4, modeled using the single-band Hubbard Hamiltonian. The physics revolves around the dynamics of photogenerated doublon-holon pairs within the Upper Hubbard Band (UHB) and Zhang-Rice Singlet (ZRS) manifolds.
key_observables: HHG spectrum (especially the global cutoff energy), time-resolved harmonic yield (low-order vs. high-order), transient reflectivity, and the charge structure factor N(k).
important_parameters: The intrinsic energy scale defined by the Hubbard bands (e.g., 4 eV cutoff), critical excitation density/fluence (e.g., F* or A0c), and the driving field strength.
main_assumptions: The analysis generalizes the three-step model of HHG to the strongly correlated Mott insulating state, and the simulations rely on mapping the physics onto the Hubbard model.
figures_summary: Figures show HHG spectra revealing a constant cutoff, time-resolved spectra comparing pre- and post-doping responses, and simulations tracking the evolution of charge correlations N(k) across critical fluence thresholds.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing HHG in Mott insulators (observing the intrinsic cutoff) to using time-resolved techniques to separate intraband/interband contributions, culminating in theoretical modeling that links spectral weight renormalization to the breakdown of spatial pair correlations.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, non-linear optical diagnostic tool (HHG) to probe subtle, many-body physics—like band reconstruction—that is typically only accessible via advanced theoretical methods, bridging quantum optics and condensed matter theory.
